 Denton council canvasses election results, District 1 runoff called for Dec. 12 
 Government Denton Denton council canvasses election results, District 1 runoff called for Dec. 12
 Explore Denton on the Impact Map stories, offers and more Natalia Young 1 min read Published November 20, 2026 at 3:00 p.m. CT Candidates Sunny Busby and Kris Cox will be on the runoff election ballot for the District 1 seat in December. ( Community Impact staff ) Denton City Council officials approved a runoff election for the District 1 seat after canvassing results of the special election during the Nov. 17 meeting .
 The details
 Candidate Sunny Busby will be running against Kris Cox, who broke a tie with opponent Michael Herron by a single vote after mail-in and provisional ballots were counted, according to previous reporting .
 Council ordered a runoff election since no candidate earned an absolute majority in the Nov. 3 election, or more than 50% of votes.
 The canvass resulted in the following breakdown of official results for the District 1 race:
 Busby: 3,196 votes (42.8%)
 Cox: 1,551 votes (20.8%)
 Herron: 1,550 votes (20.8%)
 Ward Franz: 1,178 votes (15.8%)
 The Denton County Elections Administration Building will be the only Denton polling site for both early voting and Election Day. Council chose one site to minimize expenses and avoid holiday event conflicts at the Martin Luther King Jr. Recreation Center and the Denton Civic Center.
 The runoff is expected to cost Denton $17,500 out of $205,000 allocated in the municipal budget for the fiscal year 2026-27 election expenses, according to city documents .
 The context
 A special election was called after former District 1 council member Jordan Villarreal announced he was stepping down July 30, less than three months after winning the seat in May. He ran for the position after Vicki Byrd vacated the seat to run for a trustee seat with Denton ISD, according to prior reporting .
 The District 1 seat term runs through May 2027 and will be on the ballot again during that election, according to the city’s website .
 What’s next
 Early voting for the runoff will run Nov. 30-Dec. 8, and election day will be Dec. 12. 
 Council unanimously approved including Dec. 6 as the only Sunday residents can participate in early voting, paying an additional $750 to accommodate residents who work Monday through Friday.
 The poll center will be open as follows, per the Denton County elections page :
 Nov. 30-Dec. 5, 8 a.m.-5 p.m.
 Dec. 6, 11 a.m.-5 p.m.
 Dec. 7-8, 7 a.m.-7 p.m.
